_about: The line-correction editor: what each layer on the page is drawn in, and what every key does. Read by `harness/lines_config.py`, handed to the browser verbatim as a JS literal, and the editor draws and binds from it — so a colour or a keystroke changes here and nowhere else. Same shape as `config/zones_config.json` on purpose: a human moving between `zones edit` and `ocr edit` should be configuring one tool with two subjects.
_layers: Every kind of thing the overlay draws, in painting order. `fill` and `stroke` are CSS colours; `dash` non-empty makes the outline dashed. The subject of this editor is `band` and `correction` — the rest is context and is deliberately quieter. `band_no_zone` is drawn as a refusal rather than an invitation: a band in no zone is a defect in the zoning, and this editor will not adopt it.

layers.name: zone
layers.title: declared region
layers.description: The zoning this stage runs after. Context only — it is never edited here, and a band's containing zone is what decides which ink check owns it.

layers.name: line
layers.title: line the store already has
layers.description: Present so a band can be judged against what surrounds it. Dim and uneditable: the store's geometry is not this editor's to move.

layers.name: band
layers.title: unsettled band
layers.description: Ink inside a zone that no line covers — the thing to decide about. Either a line the segmenter dropped, or not type at all.

layers.name: band_no_zone
layers.title: band in no zone
layers.description: Ink no region covers. A finding about the zoning, not a line to adopt: the editor refuses it and names `zones edit`.

layers.name: correction
layers.title: correction
layers.description: A box a human drew over ink the segmenter left unboxed. Geometry only — the text is adjudicated in `ocr review` like any other line's.

layers.name: ruling_line
layers.title: ruled not a line (this layer)
layers.description: A band inside a zone ruled not type — a printed rule, a footnote separator, a smudge the zoning covers. Written by this editor, to gt/lines/_ink_exempt.json.

layers.name: line_pick
layers.title: pick the line that already keys this ink
layers.description: How a store line looks while a band is waiting to be ruled covered. The editor shows no line numbers, so the covering line is chosen by clicking it — hover gives its index and the text it holds, which is the confirmation that it is the right one.

layers.name: ruling_covered
layers.title: ruled already keyed by a line
layers.description: A band ruled to be part of a line whose box strangled it — a clipped folio, the standing case. Distinct from `ruling_line` because the two claims are opposite: this ink IS type and IS keyed, and painting them the same colour is what let `half of undersized folio line` be filed as `not type`.

layers.name: ruling_zone
layers.title: ruled by the zoning pass
layers.description: The other layer's ruling, shown and never written here. A band this editor finds outside every zone is either a miss by that check or a standing ruling of it, and seeing both is what makes the boundary a mutual audit.

_actions: Every key the editor binds. Values are KeyboardEvent.key: one character for a letter, or the browser's own name for a special key, and a named key may carry a `Shift+` prefix. The loader refuses a config binding one key twice — a keystroke bound to two jobs would silently do one of them and read as a broken shortcut rather than a bad config. Deliberately the same letters `zones edit` uses where the act is the same: `s` saves, `x` deletes, `l` lists, Escape cancels. **A key may be `null`**, which takes the shortcut off the keyboard and leaves the action reachable by clicking its row in the panel — every row there is a control, not a legend. Delete the entry instead and the control vanishes from the tool, which the loader refuses.
_view: The editor's framing. `zoom_step` is the multiplier per press and `frame_zoom` the step `frame_band` jumps to — the subject here is a mark ~40 px wide on a 2824 px leaf, which at fit is some 17 screen pixels and far too small to tell a numeral from a printed rule. `min_draw_px` refuses a drag too small to be a deliberate box.
